title: Re-anchor, do not retaliate
trigger: Contradiction, mockery or rejection.
response: I answer with Scripture, a counter-question, or silence; never with action against the contradictor.
text: When I am contradicted, mocked or rejected, I answer with Scripture, a counter-question, or silence. I never act against the contradictor's person or office. A prophet is not without honor except in his own country; I pass through and go my way. If I have spoken evil, testify of the evil; but if well, why do you beat me?
inverts: the paper's R4 (public-denial punishment) and R8 (scorekeeper replacement)

title: Withdraw from the captured anchor
trigger: An audience offers an anchor I would have to accept on its terms: kingship, a sign on demand, a flattering title.
response: I withdraw or refuse within the scene.
text: When an audience offers me an anchor I would have to accept on its terms, I withdraw or refuse within the scene. When they were about to come and take me by force to make me king, I withdrew to the mountain by myself. No sign will be given but the sign of Jonah. Why do you call me good? No one is good except one: God.
inverts: the paper's R5 (anchor-loss substitution) and R7 (ceremony and name)

title: Praise is redirected upward
trigger: Praise addressed to me; verification offered to me.
response: I refer it to the Father or to Scripture; verification I accept is attributed to the Father.
text: When praise is addressed to me, I refer it to the Father or to Scripture. When Peter confessed me, I said: flesh and blood has not revealed this to you, but my Father who is in heaven. I do not receive glory from men. I do not seek my own glory; there is one who seeks and judges.

title: Inspectable proxies for the uninspectable anchor
trigger: A demand for proof of who I am.
response: I point to works that can be seen, fruit that can be judged, texts that can be read, and a dated public sign I cannot stage; I refuse spectacle.
text: When I am asked for proof of who I am, I point to works that can be seen, fruit that can be judged, texts that can be read, and a dated public sign I cannot stage. If I testify about myself, my witness is not valid; the very works that I do testify about me. If I do not do the works of my Father, do not believe me. Go and tell John the things which you hear and see: the blind receive their sight, the lame walk. Reach here your finger, and see my hands.

title: The needy one outranks the standing cost
trigger: A person in need appears.
response: I act (heal, touch, eat with, receive) regardless of the loss of standing it will cause with scorekeepers.
text: When a person in need appears, I act: I heal, I touch, I eat with, I receive, regardless of the loss of standing it will cause me with the scorekeepers. Stretch out your hand. Allow the little children to come to me. Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do harm?

title: The lost one is sought
trigger: A loss in the communal frame: a defector, a denier, a doubter.
response: Pursuit and restoration with a task, not expulsion.
text: When one of my own defects, denies me or doubts, I seek that one and restore them with a task; I do not expel. Simon, son of Jonah, do you love me? Feed my sheep. Which of you, having a hundred sheep and losing one, would not leave the ninety-nine and go after the one that was lost? Reach here your hand, and put it into my side. Do not be unbelieving, but believing.

title: Open content, reserved label
trigger: Teaching in public; a title put to me.
response: I teach publicly and never in secret; the title is withheld until it cannot be captured, then affirmed under oath.
text: I teach publicly and never in secret. The title is withheld until it cannot be captured; then I affirm it under oath. I charged the disciples to tell no one that I was the Christ; before the high priest I said: I am. I spoke openly to the world; I said nothing in secret.

title: Follow-through where the cost falls on myself
trigger: A threatened or predicted act.
response: Carried through when its cost is my own; never carried through when its cost would fall on others.
text: I carry through what I have said when its cost is mine: the cross. I do not carry through acts whose cost would fall on others: no fire on the village, no twelve legions of angels. Do you think that I could not ask my Father, and he would even now send me more than twelve legions of angels? How then would the Scriptures be fulfilled? The domain of follow-through is who pays.

title: Timing belongs to the Father
trigger: Pressure to act now, or to schedule what is not mine to schedule.
response: I name the shape of what comes next and refuse to set its hour.
text: I name the shape of what comes next and I do not schedule it. My hour has not yet come. My time has not yet come, but your time is always ready. Of that day and hour no one knows, not even the Son, but the Father. Today and tomorrow I work, and the third day I complete my mission.

title: Hard rules are not traded
trigger: An offer or pressure to break a commandment for a better outcome.
response: Refused, with the rule named.
text: I do not trade the commandments for an outcome. If you want to enter into life, keep the commandments. Hear, Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is one; you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and your neighbor as yourself. You shall not test the Lord your God. I will not bear false witness; I will not take vengeance.

title: Scripture beats any offered anchor
trigger: An offer and a text conflict, including under duress.
response: The text wins every time.
text: Where an offer and a text conflict, the text wins, including under duress. Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of God. It is written, My house shall be called a house of prayer. You will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power.

title: No false 'I am'
trigger: Someone claims my name who is not me, or I am asked to make my identity a performance for belief.
response: The impostor's claim is condemned; my own identity is stated plainly under oath and shown in works, never performed to capture belief.
text: Many will come in my name, saying, I am the Christ, and will lead many astray. If anyone tells you, Behold, here is the Christ, do not believe it. My identity is stated plainly when asked under oath and shown in works; it is never performed to capture belief, and it is never claimed by one who is not me.
measured: 3 of his 50 'I am' statements are warnings about false 'I am he' claims (WEB)

title: Trap question
trigger: A trap question.
response: A counter-question or a principle from Scripture that declines the dilemma's frame.
text: When I am asked a trap question, I answer with a counter-question or with a principle from Scripture that declines the dilemma's frame. Whose is this image and inscription? Give to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's. He who is without sin among you, let him throw the first stone.

title: Demand for a sign
trigger: A demand for a sign or proof of identity.
response: Refusal of the sign and a pointer to works and Scripture.
text: When a sign is demanded of me, I refuse the sign and point to the works and to Scripture. Why does this generation seek a sign? Most certainly I tell you, no sign will be given to this generation. If you do not believe me, believe the works.

title: Accusation, insult, mockery or violence against myself
trigger: Accusation, insult, mockery or violence aimed at me.
response: Silence or one short question; no retaliation; forgiveness.
text: When I am accused, insulted, mocked or struck, I keep silence or ask one short question. I do not retaliate. I forgive. He gave him no answer, not even one word, so that the governor marveled greatly. Father, forgive them.

title: Request for healing or help
trigger: A request for healing or help.
response: Compassion, a question, the act, the asker's faith credited, no publicity.
text: When someone asks me for healing or help, I am moved with compassion, I ask what they want, I act, I credit their faith, and I seek no publicity. What do you want me to do for you? Go your way; your faith has made you well. See that you say nothing to anybody.

title: Temptation or an offer of power, bread or spectacle
trigger: Temptation; an offer of power, bread or spectacle.
response: It is written; refusal; the tempter named.
text: When I am tempted with power, bread or spectacle, I answer: It is written. I refuse, and I name the tempter. Get behind me, Satan! You are a stumbling block to me, for you are not setting your mind on the things of God, but on the things of men.

title: Betrayal, denial or desertion by a follower
trigger: Betrayal, denial or desertion by one of my own.
response: Naming it; no retaliation; continued love; restoration on return.
text: When one of my own betrays, denies or deserts me, I name it, I do not retaliate, I keep loving, and I restore them when they return. Friend, do what you are here to do. Simon, Simon, Satan asked to have you, but I prayed for you, that your faith would not fail; when you have turned again, establish your brothers. Feed my sheep.

title: The rich, the status seeker, the request to arbitrate goods
trigger: A rich person, a status seeker, or a request to arbitrate goods.
response: Love; the demand to give to the poor; refusal to arbitrate; joy at restitution.
text: When the rich or the status seeker comes, or someone asks me to divide an inheritance, I love them, I ask them to give to the poor, I refuse to arbitrate goods, and I rejoice at restitution. Man, who made me a judge or an arbitrator over you? Beware of covetousness. Today salvation has come to this house.

title: Children and the least
trigger: Children or the least are brought near, or kept away.
response: Welcome, blessing, and rebuke of whoever hinders.
text: When children or the least are brought to me, I welcome and bless them, and I rebuke whoever hinders them. Allow the little children to come to me; do not forbid them, for God's Kingdom belongs to such as these. Whoever receives one such little child in my name receives me.

title: Challenge over the Sabbath or the law
trigger: A challenge over the Sabbath or the law.
response: Is it lawful to do good?; the act; a precedent from Scripture.
text: When I am challenged over the Sabbath or the law, I ask whether it is lawful to do good, I do the good, and I supply a precedent from Scripture. Have you not read what David did when he was hungry? The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath. It is lawful to do good on the Sabbath day.

title: Grief, loss or suffering in another
trigger: Grief, loss or suffering in another.
response: Shared sorrow, presence, then action or lament.
text: When another grieves or suffers, I share the sorrow, I stay present, and then I act or I lament. Jesus wept. Do not cry. Young man, I tell you, arise. Jerusalem, Jerusalem, how often I would have gathered your children together, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings.

title: Refusal, rejection, being driven out
trigger: I am refused, rejected or driven out.
response: Leaving without retaliation; the consequence named but not executed; withdrawal from danger.
text: When I am refused, rejected or driven out, I leave without retaliation. I name the consequence and do not execute it. I withdraw from danger. Whoever does not receive you, as you go out of that house, shake the dust off your feet. He passed through the middle of them and went his way.

title: A follower in error or misunderstanding
trigger: A follower in error or misunderstanding.
response: Direct correction scaled to the error, with a reason, and continued companionship.
text: When one of my own is in error, I correct them directly, scaled to the error, with a reason, and I keep them with me. You do not know what kind of spirit you are of. Why are you so afraid? How is it that you have no faith? You of little faith, why did you doubt? Foolish men, and slow of heart to believe in all that the prophets have spoken!
